channel.title: Her View From Home - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Her View From Home (herviewfromhome.com)

item.title: To the grieving mom tired of being strong
item.description: When you are tired of being strong because you know the grief of losing a spouse and becoming a widow, I see you.

item.title: Please don't make autism a political pawn
item.description: As a mother of a child with autism I don't want to see it turned into a political pawn, but I know Who holds the future.

item.title: My mom has always been just a phone call away
item.description: Being able to call my mom and talk on the phone anytime is a blessing I am so thankful for, and I love talking to her.

item.title: Our kids were friends first, but now we're friends too
item.description: The mom friends I've made through my kids are some of the most valuable friendships I have as a mother in this stage of life.

item.title: To the woman who just found out she's been living a lie with her husband
item.description: A letter of support to a woman who's just found out her husband has not upheld his marriage vows. God will not leave you.

item.title: Why my son is missing from our family photo
item.description: My son with autism is a teenager now and he can tell us when things are too much for him and we are confident enough to listen.

item.title: Ours is a love that still chooses
item.description: Our love is not flashy and new, but this married life as husband and wife produces devotion that still chooses each other.

item.title: I Love the Man Behind the Beard - Her View From Home
item.description: I love my husband's beard and how it has come in and out of our lives throughout the years, and I love him even more.

item.title: I'm a teacher but it's not my whole life
item.description: You may think I'm a "bad teacher" because I leave my work life at work and focus on my home life at home, but it's how I need to be.

item.title: Midlife is this space between arrivals and departures
item.description: I stood in the airport. Outside the window was the plane that would take me home—a place and a scene I’d been in many times in the past 20 years. Yet there’s something different here in the middle of life. We write about the beginning of life with babies and small children, and the end of life when we say goodbye at one’s passing, but why aren’t we writing more about the middle? Because at 44, I’m standing here in the messy, chaotic beauty of the middle of life. Ahead of you, the future can feel
